output:
The review is done. I found no blocking issues and three small ones, mostly about test coverage. The change sends the Transaction Service's HTTP 451 "banned Safe" response to clients with a fixed message ("Unavailable for legal reasons"). Before this change, clients got the same 451 status with the generic "An error occurred" message, so this only changes the message.

**How I ran it:** mode `--review-pr`, over `482232a40…HEAD` (one commit, `b89c2025e`, 11 files). I wrote the rule checklist to the scratchpad instead of the repo, because the checklist path isn't in `.gitignore`. I went through all 60 rules and ticked each one. I didn't need to look up the review history behind any rule. No tracked files were changed, and no tests were run.

## Rules that applied and pass

- **Scope and new files (CHANGE-01/02, PR-01):** the change stays small. The new helper sits in the existing `src/datasources/errors/helpers/` folder next to similar helpers. The new constants file is justified because Nest's `HttpStatus` has no 451.
- **Reusing existing code (REUSE-01):** everything still goes through `HttpErrorFactory`. In `TransactionApi`, the check is added once at the end of the existing `mapError` (`transaction-api.service.ts:1203`). Every catch in that file already calls `mapError`, including `isSafe` at line 250, so all of them get the new handling.
- **No leaked details (LOG-04, ROUTE-01):** the upstream `detail` text is thrown away and never forwarded. `mapBannedSafeError(error: unknown): unknown` has the same signature as the existing private `mapError`.
- **API contract (CHANGE-04):** the status stays 451; only the message changes, so this is backward-compatible.
- **Docs (PR-02):** the `docs/agents/ARCHITECTURE.md` addition matches the code: three datasources, applied before the factory reads the error.
- **Right test layer (TEST-02):** the helper has unit tests, including one through `HttpErrorFactory`. `TransactionApi.getSafe` has a unit test. There is one integration check each for the balances and safes routes. Existing tests that assert "upstream message is forwarded as-is" now exclude 451 correctly.
- **SPDX headers:** present on both new files.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Severity | File:line | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TEST-07 / TEST-09 | Medium | `src/modules/csv-export/v1/datasources/export-api.service.ts:64` | `ExportApi` now maps 451 errors, but no test at any level checks that its 451 produces the new message and code. Its spec file (`export-api.service.spec.ts:143-149`) only removes 451 from the random status codes. If someone removes the call, nothing fails. Add a test like the one for `TransactionApi.getSafe` (`transaction-api.service.spec.ts:416`). |
| 2 | TEST-07 / TEST-09 | Low | `src/modules/balances/datasources/safe-balances-api.service.ts:181`, `:221` | Of the three catch sites in `SafeBalancesApi` that were changed, only line 109 is tested, through the balances integration test (`balances.controller.integration.spec.ts:838`). The other two have no test that fails if the mapping call is removed. |
| 3 | TEST-01 / AGENTS.md non-negotiable 6 (no literal fixtures) | Low | `banned-safe.helper.spec.ts:22`, `:69`; `transaction-api.service.spec.ts:430`; `balances.controller.integration.spec.ts:857`; `safes.controller.integration.spec.ts:2426` | The fixed text `'Safe is unavailable for legal reasons'` is repeated in five places as the fake upstream `detail`. Nothing asserts on it, so `faker.lorem.sentence()` would say "this value doesn't matter" and follow the no-literal-fixtures rule. |
| 4 | REUSE-01 (tests) | Nit | `banned-safe.helper.spec.ts:36`, `export-api.service.spec.ts:144`, `transaction-api.service.spec.ts:75` | The same loop that picks a random error status other than 451 is written three times. `errorStatusCodeExcludingBannedSafe()` could become one shared test helper. |

Nothing in the checklist needs changing, and no open questions came up.
